mainEntity.name: What information and decisions do I need ready before my contractor can give me a solid addition quote?

acceptedAnswer.text:
To get a reliable quote, you need a clear scope, basic dimensions, and at least rough choices for finishes and fixtures. The more specific you are, the fewer assumptions a contractor must price.

Vague requests like “a master suite” or “bigger family room” inevitably produce wide‑ranging estimates. Sharper inputs produce tighter, more comparable bids.

Key factors:
- Sketch or description of layout and approximate size
- Desired room types and any special features (fireplace, built‑ins)
- Finish level (economy, mid‑range, or high‑end) with a few examples
- Any known constraints (must keep existing roofline, limited yard)

Make a simple written brief with your goals, rough room sizes, inspiration photos, and a candid budget range. Share it with the contractor and be ready to answer clarifying questions. A good addition contractor will help refine the scope so the quote closely matches what you actually want to build.
